children: Kering's decision to change the creative direction of its fashion house Balenciaga is "a step in the right direction," Bernstein's Luca Solca says. The French luxury-goods company parted ways with Pierpaolo Piccioli and named Martine Rose as the new creative boss of Balenciaga. Piccioli was appointed as the brand's creative chief in July last year, replacing Demna Gvasalia, who now leads Gucci's creative direction. "On paper, I see that Rose's streetwear experience and aesthetic sensibility is closer to what Balenciaga had become in consumers' minds under Demna's leadership," Solca says. Shares fall 2.5%. (andrea.figueras@wsj.com)
